title: BUTEX Science Club hosts Texverse 2.0
summary: The Bangladesh University of Textiles (BUTEX) hosted ‘Texverse 2.0’, an inter-university textile innovation and research competition, on October 30. Organized by the BUTEX Science Club, the day-long e...
content: The Bangladesh University of Textiles (BUTEX) hosted ‘Texverse 2.0’, an inter-university textile innovation and research competition, on October 30. Organized by the BUTEX Science Club, the day-long event brought together students from more than 25 public and private universities and textile colleges across Bangladesh. The event began at 8:00 am and featured eight competition categories: Maths Olympiad, Treasure Hunt, Quizard, Poster Presentation, Case Competition, AI Video Making, Article Writing and Project Exhibition. Students participated to showcase their knowledge, creativity, research capabilities and innovative ideas. A major highlight of the event was the official launch of KINKLE 2.0 , the club's second annual magazine. Professor Dr. Engr. Md. Zulhash Uddin, Vice-Chancellor of BUTEX, inaugurated the publication. The magazine aims to provide a platform for scientific thinking, research-based writing, innovative ideas and students' creative work. At the closing ceremony, Professor Dr. Engr. Md. Zulhash Uddin attended as the chief guest, while Engineer Md. Sayedur Rahman Sayed, Vice Chairman of the Textile Engineering Division of the Institution of Engineers, Bangladesh (IEB), was present as the special guest. Other guests included Professor Dr. Md. Ahashan Habib, Dean of the Faculty of Textile Management and Business Studies, BUTEX; Professor Dr. Kaniz Farhana, Head of the Department of Apparel Engineering, BUTEX; Professor Dr. Md. Mahbubor Rahman, Acting Director of Student Welfare and Head of the Department of Textile Fashion and Design, BUTEX; Shariful Islam Nayan, Manager of Redox Chemicals Limited; and Engineer S. K. title: BTTF elects Chairman and Co-Chairman at 12th Board Meeting
summary: The Bharat Tex Trade Federation (BTTF) held its 12th Board Meeting on 28th October 2026 at Le Méridien, New Delhi, during which Dr. A. Sakthivel was elected as the new… The post BTTF elects Chairman and Co-Chairman at 12th Board Meeting appeared first on The Textile Magazine .
content: The Bharat Tex Trade Federation (BTTF) held its 12 th Board Meeting on 28 th October 2026 at Le Méridien, New Delhi, during which Dr. A. Sakthivel was elected as the new Chairman and Mr. Bhadresh Dodhia was re-elected as the Co-Chairman, along with Mr. Sudhir Sekhri as the Treasurer of BTTF. Mr. Sudhir Sekhri, Treasurer, BTTF, Mr. A Sakthivel, Chairman, BTTF, Mr. Bhadresh Dodhia, Co-Chair, BTTF (Left to Right) The outgoing Chairman, Mr. Naren Goenka, and Co-Chairman, Mr. Bhadresh Dodhia, welcomed the newly elected leadership and conveyed their best wishes for the Federation’s continued growth and success. The transition marks an important step in furthering BTTF’s collective efforts to strengthen India’s position in the global textile and apparel industry. Under the new leadership, BTTF will continue to work towards advancing India’s textile and apparel export potential, enhancing the global visibility of Indian textile products, and strengthening collaboration among industry stakeholders. The new management will build on the Federation’s existing initiatives to promote India as a globally competitive sourcing and manufacturing destination, while supporting greater market access, investment, innovation and international engagement across the textile value chain. title: Global fuel prices forecast to rise 32% in 2026 amid geopolitical tensions: World Bank
summary: Key Insights Fuel prices are forecast to rise 32% in 2026. Brent crude may average $91/barrel, up from $69 in 2025. Further conflict could push Brent to $105/barrel in 2027. Global food prices may ri...
content: Key Insights Fuel prices are forecast to rise 32% in 2026. Brent crude may average $91/barrel, up from $69 in 2025. Further conflict could push Brent to $105/barrel in 2027. Global food prices may rise 18% over 2026–27. Supply disruptions could worsen global inflation and food insecurity. Global fuel prices are projected to rise by 32% in 2026, driven by escalating conflicts in the Middle East, the Russia-Ukraine war and supply disruptions, according to the World Bank’s October 2026 Commodity Markets Outlook. The report forecasts that overall commodity prices will increase by an average of 23% this year, with energy costs accounting for a significant share of the rise. Brent crude oil is expected to average $91 per barrel in 2026, up from $69 in 2025. However, prices are projected to ease to $79 per barrel in 2027 if geopolitical tensions subside and supply conditions improve. The World Bank said the conflict in the Middle East has delivered a major shock to global energy supplies. Declining oil inventories have increased the risk that further disruptions could intensify supply shortages and push prices higher. The Russia-Ukraine war has added to market pressure by disrupting energy and food supplies. Restrictions on Russia’s refined petroleum production and exports, alongside interruptions to grain shipments through the Black Sea, have further increased uncertainty in global commodity markets. Despite the expected decline in overall commodity prices in 2027, the outlook remains vulnerable to further escalation in the Middle East. Meanwhile, the World Bank warned that, under a more adverse scenario, Brent crude could average $105 per barrel in 2027, significantly above its baseline forecast of $79. title: Global oil prices surge high in six-month
summary: On 30 October, Global crude oil prices surged more than 2%, reaching their highest levels in six months as concerns over a possible escalation of the Iran conflict heightened fears of supply disruptio...
content: On 30 October, Global crude oil prices surged more than 2%, reaching their highest levels in six months as concerns over a possible escalation of the Iran conflict heightened fears of supply disruptions. Investors are increasingly worried that the conflict could worsen following the US midterm elections, raising uncertainty over global oil supplies. Brent crude futures for December delivery settled at $117.64 per barrel on 30 October, up 2.4% from the previous session. During the trading session, prices briefly climbed above $118 per barrel. Figure: Investors are increasingly worried that the conflict could worsen following the US midterm elections, raising uncertainty over global oil supplies. Meanwhile, US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude rose 2.1% to settle at $104.12 per barrel. Oil prices also recorded strong gains throughout October. Brent crude increased by 13.6% during the month, while WTI rose 15.2%, reflecting growing concerns over geopolitical risks and potential supply disruptions. Tensions surrounding oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz have further intensified market concerns. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) reported four incidents involving supertankers within a single day. According to the IRGC, two tankers were damaged by mines while travelling through routes prohibited by Iranian authorities. The Strait of Hormuz is one of the world's most important energy shipping routes, handling a significant volume of global crude oil and fuel transportation. Any conflict or security threat in the waterway could disrupt shipments and put further pressure on international oil supplies. content: The University Grants Commission (UGC) of Bangladesh plans to increase dedicated research funding for collaborative projects involving universities and industries, with a focus on practical solutions to manufacturing challenges, patent development, and commercialisation. Prof. Dr. Mamun Ahmed, Chairman of UGC, announced the initiative while addressing the 7th BUFT–CRISAT Textile Research Conference (TRC) 2026, held on October 31 at the auditorium hall of BGMEA University of Fashion and Technology (BUFT) in Nishatnagar, Turag, Dhaka. The conference brought together local and international academics, researchers, industry leaders and professionals to explore research-driven approaches to sustainability, technological advancement and industrial competitiveness in the textile and apparel sector. Addressing the conference as Chief Guest, Prof. Dr. Mamun Ahmed emphasised the need to connect academic research with real manufacturing challenges, arguing that the country's textile and apparel industry must move beyond its traditional manufacturing strengths through research, technology adoption and higher-value production. He noted that international buyers are increasingly evaluating manufacturers based on environmental performance, supply chain circularity and their ability to adopt automation and digital technologies, alongside production costs. title: Bangladesh apparel industry draws global investment for clean energy transition
summary: Key Insights Bangladesh RMG sector faces a $4.8 billion funding gap to meet 2030 climate goals. Australian clean energy delegations explore battery storage partnerships to stabilize factory power. De...
content: Key Insights Bangladesh RMG sector faces a $4.8 billion funding gap to meet 2030 climate goals. Australian clean energy delegations explore battery storage partnerships to stabilize factory power. Denmark and Sweden support a 500 MW offshore wind project off Cox's Bazar. Natural gas shortages and LNG spot prices near $30 per MMBtu raise operational costs. Rooftop solar cannot power wet processing, requiring heat recovery and electrification. Bangladesh's ready-made garment industry is partnering with global fashion brands, renewable energy companies, and international development partners to adopt solar power, offshore wind, battery storage, and energy-efficient machinery. Manufacturers are making this shift to handle high energy costs, gas shortages, and strict carbon reduction demands from international buyers. However, realizing this green transition requires substantial capital expenditure. According to LightCastle Partners, Bangladesh's RMG sector requires $6.6 billion between 2025 and 2029 to achieve a 50 percent reduction in greenhouse gas emissions by 2030. With only $1.6 billion in funding secured to date, the sector faces a massive $4.8 billion financing gap that demands urgent expansion of international climate finance, soft loans, and concessionary funding mechanisms. To bridge the financial shortfall and accelerate on-site clean energy, international solar investments and technology transfers are expanding rapidly across Bangladesh's apparel sector. Denmark's Heartland and fashion giant BESTSELLER are funding solar decarbonization models through a partnership with local cleantech venture SOLshare. summary: Danish garment maker Spectre has inaugurated a new green factory in Hung Yen Province, northern Vietnam, expanding its manufacturing footprint in the country while helping reduce greenhouse gas emissions through energy-efficient production, according to the Danish Embassy in Vietnam. The new facility, Spectre Hung Yen 2, opened at Song Tra Industrial Park in Thai Binh […] The post Danish garment firm Spectre opens $30mn green factory in northern Vietnam appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: Danish garment maker Spectre has inaugurated a new green factory in Hung Yen Province, northern Vietnam, expanding its manufacturing footprint in the country while helping reduce greenhouse gas emissions through energy-efficient production, according to the Danish Embassy in Vietnam. The new facility, Spectre Hung Yen 2, opened at Song Tra Industrial Park in Thai Binh Ward on Friday, marking the company’s fourth factory in Vietnam and second in Hung Yen. With nearly 80 years of experience in the garment industry, Spectre specializes in producing functional apparel for premium sportswear and outdoor brands. Backed by an investment of US$30 million, the new factory is expected to cut carbon dioxide emissions by approximately 1,600 metric tons annually compared with conventional factories of a similar size. It has received LEED Gold certification, the third-highest certification level under the Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design (LEED) rating system developed by the U.S. Green Building Council. The facility combines solar power with modern design solutions to improve energy efficiency and reduce its environmental footprint. It is also equipped with advanced machinery and technologies, including automation and artificial intelligence (AI) solutions, to improve production efficiency and establish higher standards across Spectre’s manufacturing operations. The factory is expected to create jobs for around 3,000 local workers. Jesper Klausen, Spectre’s co-owner and chief business development officer, said the company, was proud of its latest investment in Hung Yen. title: 12 European countries to release 42.6mn barrels of oil from strategic reserves
summary: Twelve European countries have announced plans to release 42.6 million barrels of oil from their strategic reserves by the end of January 2027 to ease concerns over global energy supplies. The release...
content: Twelve European countries have announced plans to release 42.6 million barrels of oil from their strategic reserves by the end of January 2027 to ease concerns over global energy supplies. The release will include approximately 20.5 million barrels of diesel, accounting for nearly half of the total volume. The announcement was made in a joint statement on 29 October. EU Energy Commissioner Dan Jørgensen told reporters that member states had reaffirmed their commitment to rapidly releasing the oil reserves over the coming months, with a significant portion allocated to diesel. Courtesy: Collected The participating countries are France, Germany, Italy, Belgium, Denmark, Greece, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Portugal and Sweden. The initiative is part of an agreement reached among G7 countries earlier this month. A few weeks before the latest announcement, G7 economies had announced plans to release 100 million barrels of diesel and crude oil to stabilize global supplies. The International Energy Agency (IEA) had also urged its member countries in mid-October to increase oil supplies from strategic reserves ahead of the winter season. All 12 countries participating in the latest initiative are IEA members. The move comes amid a sharp rise in global energy prices following the war involving the United States, Israel and Iran. The conflict has increased pressure on energy costs across Europe and the United States, raising concerns among consumers and policymakers. High energy prices have also become a significant political issue for the Trump administration ahead of next week's US congressional elections.
